hook.text: A dating app with no women is useless to men and vice versa. Both sides must show up for the market to work.

buildup.text: Two-sided markets connect distinct groups: buyers and sellers, riders and drivers, employers and workers.

discovery.text: The chicken-and-egg problem: you need sellers to attract buyers and buyers to attract sellers. Who comes first?

twist.text: Platforms subsidize one side to solve this. Credit cards charge merchants, not users. Uber subsidized early riders.

climax.text: Jean Tirole won the 2014 Nobel Prize for analyzing platform markets. Getting the cross-side pricing right is everything.

punchline.text: Platforms profit by solving both sides' needs.

quiz.question: What is the chicken-and-egg problem in two-sided markets?
options: Each side needs the other to come first
